target.title: fix(active-memory): recall context breaks when recent turns contain emoji
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where active-memory recall could pass malformed recent user or assistant text into the model context when the configured recent-turn snippet limit landed inside an emoji or other surrogate-pair character.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recent recall mode already bounds the amount of previous user and assistant text included in the query, but those snippets must be truncated on UTF-16-safe boundaries before becoming model-visible context. This keeps the existing limits and query shape unchanged while avoiding broken Unicode in the recall prompt.

## User Impact

Users can include emoji and other non-BMP characters in recent conversation turns without active-memory recall corrupting those characters when it builds bounded context for memory search.

## Evidence

- `origin/main` check before the fix: `extensions/active-memory/index.ts` still used raw `slice(0, params.config.recentUserChars)` and `slice(0, params.config.recentAssistantChars)` in the recent recall query path.
- Open PR search before the fix: no open PR matched `recentUserChars`, `recentAssistantChars`, active-memory recall query truncation, surrogate pair, or UTF-16 slice.
- Issue-path live proof: a temporary active-memory plugin runtime harness registered the real `before_prompt_build` hook, invoked it with recent user and assistant turns containing emoji at the configured 40-character boundary, observed the active-memory recall lane, and asserted the model-visible `Conversation context` contained bounded recent snippets without lone UTF-16 surrogates.
